data.recommendation:
Create buffbeefalo/netmambaplus-client as a fresh-root public repo populated by a source-triggered, checked, fail-closed export (candidate A), publishing via an isolated job holding a deploy key scoped to the client repo only. Alternative B (destination scheduled pull with GITHub_TOKEN) is rejected: it adds a second control plane in the destination, its selection logic lags source layout changes, GITHUB_TOKEN pushes do not trigger the client's own CI (breaking the drift-verification loop), and it adds freshness lag. Alternative C (filtered-history mirror) is rejected: auditing/filtering historical trees around the ~510 MB docs/customer media subtree is brittle and risks leaking presentation text from old commits; a fresh snapshot history excludes presentation media by construction.

Bounded contract (~6 new source-side files, zero rewrites of existing runtime code; adopting codex's paths): client/manifest.json, client/README.md (template), tools/export_client.py, tools/verify_client.py, tests/test_client_export.py, .github/workflows/client-sync.yml.

1) FAIL-CLOSED SELECTION (revised per codex). client/manifest.json enumerates explicit source-to-destination per-file mappings with no wildcards anywhere — including the frozen evidence set: each docs/customer/evidence file is individually listed with its expected sha256 (a locked inventory generated once from the current 155-file/29,266,450-byte subtree in scout.txt, then human-reviewed and frozen). Newly added or changed files — even .json/.txt/.gz under evidence — remain excluded until explicitly reviewed into the manifest. Hard-fail conditions: missing allowlisted entry; evidence-file hash mismatch against the locked inventory; any retained scientific index (artifact-index.json, packet-study pins) referencing a file not in the export; deny-set match (.mp4, .webm, .pptx, .pdf, .srt, .vtt, talk-track*, presentation*, narrate*, *video*, *course*) even for allowlisted paths; symlinks, submodules, unsafe/traversal paths, destination collisions.

2) EXPORT + EXACT BYTES + PROVENANCE. Export reads immutable Git blobs at the exact verified source-main SHA (never the working tree), preserving executable modes and raw bytes (subject to .gitattributes verification below; pin -text on exported paths if needed). Deterministic PROVENANCE.json records source repo URL, source commit, manifest sha256, exporter/policy identity, and per-file path/mode/size/sha256, plus UTC timestamp. Frozen code_sha256 pins in configs/packet-study.json (e.g. packet_data.py, tools/train_packet_model.py) are re-verified before publish and never rewritten to unblock sync; a future runtime change requires new measured evidence or an explicit historical binding. For source changes touching only excluded paths, the exporter compares payload+policy against the previous publication and no-ops without generating new provenance, retaining the prior client tip (resolves the negative-test/provenance-field conflict codex identified).

3) HISTORY. Client history starts at a new root commit containing only the reviewed export; each update is one ordinary snapshot commit on client main citing the source SHA. No source ancestry, branches, or tags are ever pushed.

4) TRIGGER + VERIFIED SOURCE MAIN (revised per codex). Sync runs on workflow_run: successful completion of the source CPU-verification workflow, restricted to canonical repository buffbeefalo/netmambaplus-reproduction and refs/heads/main; the run's exact tested SHA is confirmed against remote source main immediately before publication; PR-origin runs, stale candidates, and source-history regression/discontinuity are rejected. A manual recovery dispatch enforces identical checks. Publications are serialized (concurrency group); the destination tip is rechecked at push time and the run stops on races.

5) DRIFT PROTECTION + NON-FORCE (revised per codex). Before each update, the workflow independently regenerates the expected previous client tree from its recorded source revision and exporter/policy version, and compares the complete destination tree — paths, modes, bytes, including extra files — rejecting any unexplained destination edit or invalid provenance. Approved deletions flow through the same comparison. Publish is fast-forward git push only; client branch protection forbids force pushes. Client CI additionally re-verifies PROVENANCE.json per-file hashes on a weekly schedule.

6) SECRET/PR BOUNDARY. Export and testing run credential-free. Only an isolated final publisher job receives the client deploy key; it consumes the verified payload and never executes exported application/test code. SSH host keys and action revisions are pinned; all PR jobs are read-only (source ci.yml already declares contents: read); GitHub withholds secrets from fork PRs.

7) CLIENT CI + VERIFIER. Client CI runs the dependency-complete CPU test subset and tools/verify_client.py — a presentation-free verifier with named checks: locked evidence-inventory hashes, checkpoint-identity, prediction/aggregate result checks against retained records — verified against the exported checkout independently of the source tree. The exact check list freezes only after the truncated verify() tail / review tooling evidence lands (remaining blocker). The teaching verify_package.py is not exported: its visible verify_teaching_material()/verify_audit() require pptx/pdf/talk-track/guide artifacts.

8) README. Concise prose (prerequisites, verified asset acquisition via tools/fetch_assets.py + configs/assets.json, train/predict/evaluate commands, evidence-backed results table, limitations verbatim from configs/packet-study.json), exported from a source-side template so both repos update from one development location; clearly distinguish six-class flow results from the binary packet study, and CPU checks from GPU execution (fresh GB10 measured; other hardware unverified).

9) ACCEPTANCE + REAL UPDATE TEST. tests/test_client_export.py exercises the actual implementation against temporary bare repos: deterministic output and source-blob equality; missing-dependency rejection; untracked/presentation exclusion; unsafe-path rejection; updates and approved deletions; unchanged-input no-op; injected destination drift rejected; stale/unverified/PR-source rejection; concurrent destination change stops publication. Then a live end-to-end test: merge one allowlisted documentation change through source main; after source CI succeeds, verify the client gained exactly one non-force commit whose PROVENANCE.json cites the new SHA, changed bytes are sha256-identical, frozen evidence unchanged, client CI green; verify the negative case (denied-only change → retained prior publication, no new provenance); inspect every destination-history tree for forbidden files; exercise the retained train/predict commands from a clean client checkout with assets on appropriate hardware. Record both workflow-run and commit IDs.

FREEZE GATE. The manifest, the runnable closure (fetch/requirements/tests subset), and the verifier check list freeze only after the requested evidence lands; until then those three items are open blockers, not architecture questions. Repo/key provisioning and the live update test are performed by the authorized executor session, not this council context.

data.recommendation:
Converge on source-triggered checked export with a dedicated client-only deploy key. Destination scheduled pull with GITHUB_TOKEN remains viable if it verifies source main and tests before pushing; token event suppression does not invalidate that design. It removes the persistent write key but adds scheduler maintenance and workflow-update handling. Filtered history need not require recurring force pushes, but requires substantially more historical-content auditing than a fresh-root export. Two evidence blockers below still prevent freezing the exact runnable inventory and scientific checks.

Bounded source changes: add or update client/manifest.json, client/README.md, client/ci.yml, client/.gitattributes, tools/export_client.py, tools/verify_client.py, tests/test_client_export.py, and .github/workflows/client-sync.yml. Keep existing runtime code and frozen scientific records unchanged. Map the client templates to README.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml and .gitattributes. Inspect existing paths before implementation: the supplied grep already references tests/test_client_export.py.

The manifest must enumerate individual reviewed paths and destination mappings, including runtime dependencies, selected tests and scientific records. No evidence-directory wildcard or extension-based automatic admission. Missing entries, unsafe paths, collisions, symlinks, submodules and forbidden presentation/media paths fail. Unlisted files stay excluded. Retaining tools/build_cuda.py requires tools/build_gb10.py, as the visible import establishes; the remaining closure requires inspection.

Read immutable Git blobs at the verified source SHA, preserve bytes and executable modes, and generate deterministic PROVENANCE.json containing source identity, manifest/exporter identities and payload hashes, sizes and modes. The client attribute template must disable checkout conversions; exclude competing nested attribute files and verify clean-checkout byte equality. Preserve frozen indexes and measurement pins. Publication must fail on unexplained pin mismatches; changed runtime code needs an explicitly reviewed historical measurement binding or new evidence, never silently rewritten pins. Compare payload and effective policy before generating new provenance: an excluded-only change leaves the existing client commit and provenance unchanged.

Trigger on successful completion of the identified source CPU-verification workflow. Validate canonical repository, push-to-main origin, exact tested SHA and successful verification; reject PR-origin, stale and unverified candidates. Require source ancestry continuity and recheck remote main immediately before publication. Manual recovery uses the same gate. Export, reconstruct the previous publication and test without the destination credential. Only an isolated final publisher receives the deploy key; it consumes the verified payload without executing exported application or test code. Restrict the remote and branch, pin action revisions and SSH host keys, and keep PR jobs read-only.

Create a fresh client root without source ancestry or tags. Before updates, independently regenerate the previous expected export using its validated source revision and recorded policy, then compare the complete destination tree, including extra paths and modes. Reject drift or incompatible policy reconstruction. Serialize publication, recheck the destination tip, and push one ordinary fast-forward commit; stop on races and never force-push. Repository provisioning must verify the client's actual settings and key scope.

Acceptance: run the actual exporter/publication implementation against temporary bare repositories, covering deterministic output, source-byte equality, checkout transforms, exclusions, missing dependencies, unsafe paths, updates, deletions, no-ops, destination drift, stale/unverified/PR candidates and publication races. Test the exported tree independently of the source checkout. Its CI must run the dependency-complete selected CPU tests and the agreed scientific verifier; provenance hashes alone do not validate measured results. Keep setup, executable commands, results and limitations concise, distinguishing six-class flow results from the binary packet study and CPU checks from measured GPU execution.

The authorized calling session or trusted automation performs provisioning and the real update test: after initial publication, merge a useful client-README change through source main, allow successful source CI to trigger publication automatically, and record source/client commits, workflow runs, exact changed-file bytes, unchanged frozen evidence and passing client CI. Audit destination-history trees for forbidden content. These external actions are outside the read-only council and broker participant roles.

Resolved checkout-transform concerns through a client-specific attribute template, raw-blob construction and clean-checkout hash verification; copying unseen source attributes is unnecessary.

Resolved the provenance/no-op conflict: exclude volatile timestamps and retain the previous publication when payload and effective policy are unchanged.
Treat current remote-main status and repository settings as enforced provisioning/publication preconditions, not architectural blockers.
Scheduled pull remains a valid alternative, and filtered history does not inherently require force pushes. These corrections do not change the preferred architecture.
